history.summary: Large 1,012 sqft 2BR at The Jade, a 2004 D23 leasehold just 160m from Bukit Batok MRT (NSL). Good 5.5%/yr resale CAGR on 39 txns, but priced at $1,482 psf vs $1,428 median (~4% above) and the unit is oversized for a 2BR, inflating quantum to $1.5M.
history.rating_rationale: The 160m-to-MRT location and solid 5.5%/yr resale CAGR (39 txns) are genuine positives. However it's priced ~4% above the $1,428 median, the 2004 build is 22 years old with a ~78yr lease, and the 1,012 sqft for a 2BR makes the per-unit quantum ($1.5M) high relative to the rental a 2BR commands — depressing yield. Score_1000 of 520 reflects this balance. Liquid Bukit Batok location keeps it from Avoid, but the above-median pricing and age cap it at Neutral.

history.summary: A 1,475sf 3BR+study at The Jade (Sim Lian, 2004, 280 units, 1 block, 99yr from 2001 — 74yr left) 160m from Bukit Batok MRT, asking $2.40M / $1,627psf. The exact layout has 9 URA resales; the 2025-26 prints are $1.99M-$2.20M ($1,349-$1,492psf), the best being $2.20M (fl 11-15, Mar-26). The ask is ~9% above the highest-ever print for this layout and ~13% above the project's typical — and an identical 1,475sf unit is live on PropertyGuru right now at $2.25M. Even the bigger 1,615sf unit on fl 26-30 sold for only $2.38M (Oct-25). Rent here is ~$5.1-5.6k, which is 1.5% net. There's no discount, no carry, and a shortening lease.
history.rating_rationale: The price is the problem. $2.40M ($1,627psf) is above every print for this exact 1,475sf layout: 2025-26 resales were $1.99M, $2.12M and $2.20M ($1,349-$1,492psf), so fair value from its own prints is ~$2.10-2.25M depending on floor. That is 7-12% below the ask. A same-size unit is listed at $2.25M right now, and a larger 1,615sf high-floor unit sold for $2.38M in Oct-25. The 'price raised' history ($2.25M→$2.40M) is the unit-group artifact: that chain pools several agents' listings of the same size, not one seller raising the price. The project's fundamentals are fine but not strong enough to excuse overpaying. It is OCR and 160m from Bukit Batok MRT/West Mall, with a deep, profitable resale record (REALSCORE 3.2, 88.5% of 282 resale pairs profitable, ~4.5%/yr). Against that: net yield is 1.5%, the lease is 74yr (~67 at exit, which erodes the CPF/financing buyer pool), and the building is a 22-year-old single block. score_1000 419 agrees, driven by age_value −15, psf_value −5.5 and yield −6. The mandate fits (hers, ≈$2.5M, 3-4BR). At ≤$2.15M (≈$1,460psf, in line with the Mar-26 print) this would be a Neutral. At $2.40M it is an Avoid.

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: URA 3BR contracts at The Jade (1,300-1,400sf band, 2025-26) cluster $4.9k-$5.9k; $5,100 estimate is fair, a 1,475sf 3BR+study might fetch ~$5.3-5.6k. Gross ~2.6-2.8%, net ~1.5% — carry only, no investment case from yield.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: The 1,475sf layout printed $1,104-1,226psf in 2022 and $1,349-1,492psf in 2025-26, so it has risen ~5%/yr, in line with the ura_5yr_cagr of 5.44%. That is trailing, bull-regime momentum, and the model gives it no forward weight. The forward drivers are neutral-to-negative. Buying above its own prints means the first 7-12% of any appreciation just gets back to fair value, and the lease drops below 70yr during the hold. Expect roughly market-rate growth at best from fair value, less from this ask.
agent_evaluation.stack_notes: No profile; floor level not published by the listing. Project is a single 280-unit block (Sim Lian, Design Link Architects), 16 layouts 1,011-3,881sf; the 1,475sf type is the 3BR+study. Recent prints show floor premia are modest (fl 06-10 $1,349-1,438psf vs fl 11-15 $1,492psf) — no floor plausibly supports $1,627psf.
